To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have detected RV variations up the ~5 m/s for M dwarfs that we attribute to activity cycles and we found that only 36% stars with activity cycles have RV variations.

(i) we found a strong correlation between the activity level of M dwarfs and their CCF parameters; (ii) we found a weak correlation between RV and activity level; and (iii) we did not find any correlation between RV and the activity cycle period.
(i) M-dwarfs show long-term RV variations that are likely due to activity cycles; and (ii) the fraction of M-dwarfs showing such variations is smaller than for K-dwarfs, but the amplitude is larger.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the detection of correlations between activity cycles and RV variations for a sample of M dwarf stars.
the long-term magnetic activity of 27 M dwarfs, and its impact on the RV measurements of these stars.
the detection and study of the magnetic cycles of a sample of 25 M dwarfs from the HARPS planet search survey.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the RV variations induced by magnetic activity cycles in M dwarfs is not a problem for planet detection with current instruments, but that this effect should be taken into account in future RV instruments.
M dwarfs do show RV variations due to stellar activity, but that these variations are less frequent than for K dwarfs.
magnetic cycles are not a serious problem for M dwarfs, but they are a serious problem for K dwarfs.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the activity of M dwarfs is not as well correlated to the RV as it is for K dwarfs.
the RV variations of M dwarfs due to magnetic cycles are less significant compared to those of K dwarfs.
the RV of M dwarfs is not affected by magnetic cycles as much as that of K dwarfs.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the RV of M dwarfs is affected by activity cycle variations, and that the RV variations are not necessarily correlated with the activity level.
, while the RV variations induced by magnetic activity are not as large as those observed in K dwarfs, they are not negligible either.
the RV variations induced by magnetic cycles in M dwarfs are smaller than in K dwarfs, and therefore, the impact of magnetic cycles on the search for Earth-mass planets is smaller.
